title: Fluid pressure & upthrust
examples: What is the relationship between depth and pressure?
How can I calculate the upthrust on an object?
Does the object's weight matter when it floats?

explain.say: Today we will explore fluid pressure and the concept of upthrust. Say the formula for fluid pressure. It is p equals rho g h.
The pressure at a depth depends on the fluid's density, gravity, and the depth. Say the units for pressure in this context. They are usually pascals.
Archimedes discovered that the upthrust equals the weight of the fluid displaced. Say this is a very important principle. It helps explain why things float.
An object floats when the upthrust pushing up equals the object's weight pulling down. Say this is the condition for floating. Think of a boat on water.

faq.q: Why is the pressure greater at the bottom of a pool?
faq.a: The pressure increases with depth because you are pushing down through more fluid. It depends on how deep you go.
Upthrust is the upward force exerted by a fluid on an object submerged in it. It is the fluid pushing up on the object.

faq.q: Does the object need to be fully submerged to float?
faq.a: No, an object can float while only partially submerged. The upthrust only needs to equal the weight.

faq.q: Does the density of the fluid matter for upthrust?
faq.a: Yes, the density of the fluid is a key part of the calculation. A denser fluid creates more upthrust.
asks: How does fluid density affect buoyancy?

faq.q: Is the upthrust always directed upwards?
faq.a: Yes, by definition, the upthrust force exerted by the fluid is always directed vertically upwards. It is a supporting force.
asks: What is the direction of upthrust?

facts: Fluid pressure increases with depth in a fluid.
The formula for pressure at depth is p equals rho g h.
Archimedes' principle states upthrust equals the weight of displaced fluid.
An object floats when the upthrust equals its own weight.

quiz.say: A block is submerged in oil. If the depth increases, what happens to the pressure?

options.show: Pressure is proportional to the surface area.
options.say: Pressure is proportional to the surface area.

quiz.why: The formula p equals rho g h shows that pressure increases as h, or depth, increases.

wrong.0: This is wrong because pressure is dependent on the depth of the fluid.
wrong.1: This is wrong because gravity pulls the fluid, increasing the pressure deeper down.
wrong.2: This is wrong because pressure depends on depth, not the surface area of the container.

quiz.say: If the upthrust on an object equals its weight, what is the object doing?
quiz.why: When the upward upthrust matches the downward weight, the object is suspended or floating.

wrong.0: Acceleration upwards requires the upthrust to be greater than the weight.
wrong.1: The object is experiencing two equal and opposite forces, not zero net force.
wrong.3: Sinking happens when the weight is greater than the upthrust.

quiz.say: A boat floats in seawater. If the boat's weight increases, what happens to the upthrust required?
quiz.why: For the boat to remain floating, the upward upthrust must always balance the total weight.

wrong.0: This would cause the boat to sink because the forces would no longer balance.
wrong.1: If the weight changes, the required upthrust must also change to maintain equilibrium.
wrong.2: The boat only sinks if the upthrust cannot increase enough to match the new weight.
